title: Perimeter, Area and Volume
seo_title: Grade 4 Perimeter, Area and Volume Worksheets with Answers (CAPS Maths)
standard_text: Measure perimeter using rulers or measuring tapes; find areas of regular and irregular 2-D shapes by counting squares on grids; find volume/capacity of objects by packing or filling them.
meta_desc: Free CAPS Grade 4 perimeter, area and volume worksheets: adding sides, perimeter on grids, area by counting squares, estimating area and volume by counting cubes. 100 questions with memos.
key_big: Perimeter: around. Area: inside. Volume: space filled.
key_sub: Count squares for area and cubes for volume.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Perimeter is the distance all the way around a shape. Add the lengths of all the sides.
  • Area is the space inside a shape. Count the squares that cover it (square units).
  • Volume is the space a 3-D object takes up. Count the cubes that fill it (cubic units).
  • Count hidden cubes too: a layer of 3 × 2 cubes, 2 layers high, has 12 cubes.

Examples

Example

Rectangle 6 cm by 4 cm

perimeter 6 + 4 + 6 + 4 = 20 cm

area 6 × 4 = 24 squares

Answer: 20 cm and 24 cm²

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Squares for perimeterPerimeter counts edges, not squares.
Only two sidesA rectangle has 4 sides.
Visible cubes onlyCount the hidden cubes in each layer.

items.q: A four-sided card has four sides: 12 cm, 9 cm, 15 cm and 10 cm. What is its perimeter?
items.e: Add all 4 sides: 12 + 9 + 15 + 10 = 46 cm. Every side counts, even when they are all different.

items.q: A rectangle is 15 cm long and 7 cm wide. What is its perimeter?
items.e: A rectangle has 2 long sides and 2 short sides: 15 + 7 + 15 + 7 = 44 cm. Adding only 15 + 7 = 22 leaves out two sides.

items.q: What is the area of the shaded shape?
items.e: Count the shaded squares, row by row: there are 12, so the area is 12 squares. Count each square once.

items.q: What is the area of the shaded rectangle?
items.e: Count the squares inside: 3 rows of 5 squares. 3 × 5 = 15 squares. (16 is the number of 1-unit sides around the edge: that is the perimeter.)

items.q: What is the area of the shaded house shape? Two half squares make one whole square.

items.q: You estimate the area of a curved shape on a squared grid. Which squares do you count?
c: Whole and half or more covered
items.e: Count every whole square, and count a square as 1 if half or more of it is covered. Leave out squares that are less than half covered. The bits you count and leave out roughly balance.

items.q: Each square is 1 cm². Which shape has the largest area?
items.e: Count the squares in each shape: A 10, B 8, C 7, D 9. Shape A has the largest area (10 cm²).

items.q: Each square is 1 cm². Which shape has the smallest area?
items.e: Count the squares in each shape: A 9, B 7, C 11, D 8. Shape B has the smallest area (7 cm²).

items.q: Each shape has an area of 10 cm². Which shape has the longest perimeter?
items.e: Count the 1 cm sides around each shape: A 14 cm, B 16 cm, C 18 cm, D 14 cm. The same area can have different perimeters. Shape C has the longest (18 cm).

items.q: This is the plan of an L-shaped garden bed. How much edging goes all the way around it?
items.e: Missing side: 13 − 7 = 6 m. Add all 6 sides: 6 + 4 + 7 + 3 + 13 + 7 = 40 m.

items.q: A rectangular flower bed has a perimeter of 30 m. One side is 9 m long. How long is the side next to it?
items.e: The two 9 m sides make 18 m. 30 − 18 = 12 m for the other two sides, so each is 12 ÷ 2 = 6 m. Check: 9 + 6 + 9 + 6 = 30 m.

items.q: At the athletics day warm-up, Tebogo jogs 2 times around a rectangular field. The field is 60 m long and 40 m wide. How far does he jog?
items.e: Once around: 60 + 40 + 60 + 40 = 200 m. Two times around: 2 × 200 = 400 m.

items.q: Busisiwe’s bedroom floor is 4 m by 3 m. Carpet squares are 1 m by 1 m. How many carpet squares cover the floor?
items.e: 3 rows of 4 squares: 3 × 4 = 12 carpet squares, so the area is 12 m². 14 is the perimeter in metres (4 + 3 + 4 + 3).

items.q: The teacher has 20 carpet squares. Each is 1 m². The reading corner needs 4 rows of 4 squares. How many carpet squares are left over?
items.e: Reading corner: 4 rows of 4 = 16 squares. Left over: 20 − 16 = 4 squares.

items.q: Liam’s family builds a square chook pen with sides of 6 m. Each fence panel is 2 m long. How many panels go all the way around?
items.e: Perimeter: 6 + 6 + 6 + 6 = 24 m. Each panel is 2 m: 24 ÷ 2 = 12 panels.

items.q: Ayanda’s family is building a garden bed 4 m long and 2 m wide. How much timber edging goes all the way around it?
items.e: The edging goes along all 4 sides: 4 + 2 + 4 + 2 = 12 m.

items.q: A classroom floor plan is drawn on a grid. Each square is 1 m². The floor covers 30 whole squares and 4 half squares. What is the area of the floor?
items.e: Two half squares make one whole square, so 4 half squares make 2. Area: 30 + 2 = 32 m².

items.q: Lethabo glues ribbon around the edge of a photo frame. The frame is 20 cm long and 15 cm wide. How much ribbon does he need?
items.e: Ribbon goes around the edge, so find the perimeter: 20 + 15 + 20 + 15 = 70 cm.

items.q: A classroom floor is covered with square carpet tiles. Each tile is 1 m long and 1 m wide. There are 7 rows of 9 tiles. What is the area of the floor?
items.e: Each tile is 1 m², so count the tiles: 7 rows of 9 is 7 × 9 = 63 m².

items.q: Each small cube is 1 cubic unit. What is the volume of this prism?
items.e: Each layer has 3 rows of 5 cubes = 15 cubes. There are 2 layers: 15 × 2 = 30 cubic units. Count the cubes you cannot see, too (only 22 cubes show a face).

items.q: The bottom layer of a bin has 7 rows of 4 unit cubes. The bin holds 5 layers. How many unit cubes fill it?
items.e: One layer: 7 × 4 = 28 cubes. 5 layers: 28 × 5 = 140 cubes.

items.q: The bottom layer of a box has 4 rows of 6 unit cubes. The box holds 3 layers. How many unit cubes fill it?
items.e: One layer: 4 × 6 = 24 cubes. 3 layers: 24 × 3 = 72 cubes.

items.q: The layers of this prism are pulled apart. How many unit cubes are in the whole prism?
items.e: One layer: 3 × 3 = 9 cubes. 2 layers: 9 × 2 = 18 cubes.

items.q: How many unit cubes are in the bottom layer of this prism?
items.e: The bottom layer is 5 cubes across and 4 cubes deep: 5 × 4 = 20 cubes. The front face shows 5 × 2 = 10 cubes, but that is not a layer.
